clue.text: Scoff up, kidder!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for scoff is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to scoff at is to rail against

explanation.surface: Someone tells a teaser to drink up their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAIL, a synonym of scoff, to read LIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who kids you is telling you untruths, a fibber.

clue.text: Opening supporter's proverbially third in secret

definitions.meaning: a post from which a field gate swings
the saying 'between you, me and the post at the gate' makes it the third party to a confidence

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal post holding a gate, plus the proverbial silent witness in 'between you, me and the gatepost'.

clue.text: Right space on ancient vessel for observation

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
Noah's ark, an ancient ship

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a berth on an old ship for watching from.
explanation.walkthrough: EM is a printing term: a space the width of the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an observation is a comment, something said in passing.

clue.text: Uncommonly nice — else who would be a publican?

indicators.note: uncommonly suggests the letters appear in an unusual order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering who would ever choose to run a pub if it were not so very pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommonly' rearranges NICE and ELSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A British publican holds the licence to sell alcohol on the premises.

clue.text: Bishop holds one captivated by "Primate With Sword"

indicators.note: the bishop's letters hold the rest within them, a container signal

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: being captivated, the numeral is held prisoner inside the primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bishop is enthralled by a painting called Primate With Sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivated by' gives APIE (the numeral inside the ape). 'Primate' looks like a church title beside Bishop, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed thrusting sword.

clue.text: Playfully modest about 50? It can be a bit much

indicators.note: the modest word goes around the number, a container signal

parts.note: coy means pretending shyness in a playful way
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone asks if feigned shyness around one's fiftieth birthday is overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside COY.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloy is to become sickly through excess, as overly sweet food does.

clue.text: Obsessed when taking cab back, having dined out

indicators.note: dined out: the eating word sits outside the vehicle, a container signal

parts.note: fed means having had a meal

indicators.note: back means the word for cab is read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on catching a taxi home after a restaurant meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives IXAT. 'dined out' looks like eating at a restaurant, but 'out' puts the eating word around the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being fixated means having an obsessive attachment or preoccupation.

clue.text: Wonder if motor reverses within the distance

indicators.note: within places the car inside the distance word

parts.note: a mile is the standard British unit of distance

indicators.note: reverses means the motor word is read backwards

parts.note: a motor is a car

explanation.surface: Amazing if a car manages to reverse inside the required distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses' gives RAC, itself the name of a British motoring club, which helps the motoring surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wonder is an extraordinary, seemingly impossible event.

clue.text: Some swear blind about bank

indicators.note: about means the run is turned round
some of the phrase means just a run of its letters is taken

explanation.surface: Some people swear blind about a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes EARB from swEAR Blind; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish word: a brae is a hillside or steep bank, often by a river.

clue.text: Arty suite redesigned for plain living

indicators.note: redesigned implies the furniture letters are given a new layout

explanation.surface: An artistic set of furniture is remade for a simple life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges ARTY and SUITE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerity is a simple, frugal way of life without luxuries.

clue.text: Bridge player at club showing hesitation to one who speaks incoherently

parts.note: South, S, is one of the four players at bridge
a putter is a golf club
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A card player at a club hesitates in front of someone who mumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a card club next to Bridge, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: To sputter is to speak in an explosive, stumbling way, so a sputterer talks that way.

clue.text: Parishioners come together

definitions.meaning: a congregation regarded as a priest's charge of sheep

explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a pastor's congregation, and a verb for gathering in numbers.

clue.text: Cut down endlessly over one who breaks the law

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the cut word is dropped

parts.note: to fell a tree is to cut it down
on means about, over a subject

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker is chopped down for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last L of FELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone who has committed a serious crime.

clue.text: Against the current higher school grouping

parts.note: up means higher
a stream is a class of pupils grouped by ability in British schools

explanation.surface: Contrarian pupils placed in a top set.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools, a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: going upstream means moving against the flow of a river.

clue.text: Pester girl with Scottish grandchild

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
oy is a Scots word for a grandchild

explanation.surface: A grandmother is badgered by a Scottish grandchild.
explanation.walkthrough: OY (also oe) is a Scots dialect word for a grandchild.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to annoy someone is to irritate or badger them.

clue.text: Palm found in worker's accommodation?

parts.note: a flat is a place to live
a ... is a worker, so worker's means belonging to the ...

explanation.surface: A palm tree spotted in a labourer's lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Hand is a worker, as in farmhand, so 'worker's' reads as 'of the hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is the flat inner surface of one's hand.

clue.text: See 15
A butcher's examination?

parts.note: butcher's hook is rhyming slang for look, so a butcher's is a quick look

explanation.walkthrough: British rhyming slang: 'have a butcher's' (hook = look) means take a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, cursory inspection, a single glance over something.

clue.text: See 15
Where I come from hot women get spoilt

indicators.note: letters that get spoilt are messed up, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: In my home area the attractive women are pampered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get spoilt' rearranges HOT WOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: One's home town is the place one comes from, where one grew up.

clue.text: One partly chosen for certain compelling qualities

definitions.text: One partly chosen for certain compelling qualities

indicators.note: partly means only part of these words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A recruit picked for particular persuasive traits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes the letters from chosEN FOR CERtain, and the whole clue describes such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An enforcer is someone who compels obedience, often hired for toughness.

clue.text: Elaborate talk about opening night

indicators.note: the talk word goes around the night letter, a container signal

parts.note: orate means to talk at length

indicators.note: opening takes the first letter of night

explanation.surface: Grand speeches on a first night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' gives N, the start of night; 'about' puts ORATE round it. 'opening night' looks like a theatre premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ornate means highly decorated, elaborate in design.

clue.text: Fellow claiming decoration lacks bite

indicators.note: claiming means the fellow takes hold of the medal, enclosing it

parts.note: a guy is a fellow
MM, the Military Medal, is a British decoration

explanation.surface: A man claims a medal he did not earn but is toothless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decoration' suggests ornament, but it is a medal for bravery; the man holds it in his grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Gummy describes a toothless mouth, all gums, which therefore cannot bite.

clue.text: Of whom 1 in 3 at the wedding were buttonholed, poetically

definitions.text: Of whom 1 in 3 at the wedding were buttonholed, poetically

parts.words: Of whom 1 in 3 at the wedding were buttonholed, poetically
parts.note: in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, the mariner 'stoppeth one of three' wedding visitors to tell his tale

explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like references to 1 and 3 down but mean 'one of three'; buttonholed means accosted, not given a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: People invited to a wedding, as in the poem's famous wedding scene.

clue.text: Large gathering for Tory to give a damn about nothing

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: the cursing word goes about the zero, a container signal

parts.note: to curse is to say damn
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A big crowd assembles for a Conservative to swear about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside CURSE to make COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a large crowd assembled, or the open space where crowds gather.

clue.text: Sure thing, if it's dead

definitions.meaning: a certainty, something bound to happen
with dead in front it makes a British phrase for a racing certainty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead cert' is British slang for a certainty, especially a racing tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form of certainty: something sure to happen, especially a horse sure to win.

clue.text: Being apt to turn, fathead spat

indicators.note: to turn means the apt word is read backwards

parts.note: fit means suitable, apt
the head of the word fat is its first letter

explanation.surface: An idiot spits when about to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' gives TIF. 'fathead' is split: the head of 'fat', not an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, a minor tiff between friends.

clue.text: Animal up for run

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the animal is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a wolf is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature ready for a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: liquid that flows runs, as a river does.

clue.text: Old-fashioned "please" becoming tripe, eh?

indicators.note: becoming means the letters turn into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Asking politely sounds silly when it comes out as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges TRIPE and EH.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic contraction of 'I pray thee', used to mean please.

clue.text: Leading ditherers back to cooker

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: top means leading, foremost
wets are feeble, indecisive people, in British slang

explanation.surface: The most indecisive people get sent back to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TOPWETS into the answer; 'wets' is British slang for weaklings.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewpot is a pot for cooking stews in.
